conclusions.question: 4.5: Which PyMongo pins can use AsyncMongoClient against engine 1.2.0?
conclusions.answer: pymongo 4.8.0 cannot: `from pymongo import AsyncMongoClient` raises ImportError (cannot import name 'AsyncMongoClient' from 'pymongo'). pymongo 4.9, 4.11 and 4.13.0 import it (pymongo.asynchronous.mongo_client.AsyncMongoClient, no import warning) and each got ping {'ok': 1.0} on admin and t_drivers, server_info version 7.0.0, and a working async insert/find/delete. The sync ping control passed for all four pins. On this engine the import is the only floor among these pins: 4.9 is the first release with the API and 4.13 the GA release (beta/GA status per DECISIONS 4.5); the engine adds no further floor.

conclusions.question: 4.6: Does Beanie 2 (pip install "beanie>=2,<3") complete init/insert/find/delete on AsyncMongoClient against engine 1.2.0?
conclusions.answer: Yes. pip resolved beanie 2.2.0 + pymongo 4.20.2 + pydantic 2.14.4 with no motor. Its metadata requires pymongo>=4.11.0,!=4.15.0,<5.0.0. init_beanie on AsyncMongoClient (listIndexes returned code 26 NamespaceNotFound on the new collection, which PyMongo treats as no indexes, then createIndexes created it), insert, find_one, find().to_list(), get, delete (deleted_count 1) and count (0) all succeeded with no Python warnings.

conclusions.question: 4.6: Does pip install "beanie<2" pull Motor?
conclusions.answer: Yes. It resolves beanie 1.30.0, whose runtime requirement motor>=2.5.0,<4.0.0 pulls motor 3.7.1 ('Collecting motor<4.0.0,>=2.5.0 (from beanie<2)'). Motor in turn pulls pymongo 4.20.2 ('pymongo<5.0,>=4.9 (from motor...)'). pip show reports beanie Requires motor, motor Required-by beanie, and pymongo Required-by motor.

conclusions.question: Does Beanie 1 + Motor (as resolved today) still work against engine 1.2.0?
conclusions.answer: Yes. The same round trip through motor.motor_asyncio.AsyncIOMotorClient succeeded (beanie 1.30.0, motor 3.7.1, pymongo 4.20.2). The only difference from Beanie 2 was 4 PydanticDeprecatedSince211 warnings from lazy_model/parser/new.py:107 (lazy-model 0.2.0, which Beanie 1 pins exactly). Motor raised no warning.

conclusions.question: Were the Beanie 1/Motor failures seen in earlier sample runs ('MotorDatabase object is not callable'; cannot import name '_QUERY_OPTIONS' from 'pymongo.cursor') caused by the engine?
conclusions.answer: Probably not. A fresh unpinned beanie<2 resolution works against the engine, and those errors are client-library mismatches. Those samples' exact pins were not re-run here, so this stays inferred.

conclusions.question: EXTRA: Is it safe to call init_beanie again on every app restart against engine 1.2.0?
conclusions.answer: With the default allow_index_dropping=False, yes. Beanie re-sends createIndexes for name_1 on every init, and the engine answers ok with note 'all indexes already exist', so there is no conflict even though listIndexes adds storageEngine {enableOrderedIndex: true}. With allow_index_dropping=True, no. Both Beanie 2.2.0 and 1.30.0 sent dropIndexes name_1 (reply nIndexesWas 2) and then createIndexes name_1 (numIndexesBefore 1, numIndexesAfter 2) for an unchanged model. So every restart with that flag drops and rebuilds each Beanie-declared secondary index.

conclusions.question: EXTRA: Why does allow_index_dropping=True rebuild unchanged indexes on this engine, and would MongoDB do the same?
conclusions.answer: In the installed Beanie source (beanie/odm/fields.py, IndexModelField), index equality compares every option except 'key' and 'v'. The engine adds storageEngine {enableOrderedIndex: true} to the secondary indexes it lists: name_1 here, and the TTL and partial-unique indexes in the 0.117 ttl-semantics and partial-unique reports. So the listed index never equals the declared one. A server that lists only the options Beanie sent would compare equal and drop nothing. That half was not tested here (no MongoDB server). A kit or Learn note should say: do not run Beanie with allow_index_dropping=True against DocumentDB, or expect an index rebuild per start.

conclusions.question: Did any engine-dependent result change between engine 0.117 (first run) and 1.2.0?
conclusions.answer: No. The same versions resolved and every pin and both Beanie lines had the same outcome. This run also checked more than the 0.117 run did (see comparison note).

conclusions.question: Do these results prove managed Azure DocumentDB behaviour?
conclusions.answer: No. They are observations of the open-source engine 1.2.0 and its gateway in documentdb-local: one node, SCRAM-SHA-256 only, TLS with a self-signed certificate, and retryWrites=false in the URI. The managed service may run a different engine or gateway build. The AsyncMongoClient, Beanie and storageEngine/allow_index_dropping results need a managed-cluster check before Learn or the kit quotes them as service behaviour.

conclusions.question: 4.11-open: what floors does this evidence support stating in kit text?
conclusions.answer: Maintainer decision. The evidence supports gating AsyncMongoClient on pymongo>=4.13 (GA); 4.9 and 4.11 import and work here but predate GA (4.10 and 4.12 were not tested). It also supports stating that Beanie 2 needs pymongo>=4.11,!=4.15.0 and no Motor, and that `pip install "beanie<2"` silently installs Motor (3.7.1 today), which topic 4.7 records as past end of life on May 14, 2026. The allow_index_dropping caveat above is a new item for the Beanie guidance.

notes: Pins were installed exactly as specified (pymongo==4.8.0, ==4.9, ==4.11, ==4.13); ==4.9 / ==4.11 / ==4.13 resolve to the first release of each line (4.9, 4.11, 4.13.0), which is what a floor test needs.
pip served every file from its local cache; the 4.8.0 cp313 wheel in that cache was built locally from the official sdist because PyPI publishes no cp313 wheel for 4.8.0.

Steps marked EXTRA go beyond the spec: an async CRUD round trip per pymongo pin, Beanie get/count, a restart re-init, an allow_index_dropping re-init, and wire capture through pymongo command monitoring (allowlisted data and index commands only; authentication commands are never recorded).

The scripts were iterated during this session: warning capture was added to probe_pymongo.py, and the re-inits and wire capture to probe_beanie.py. Every output in out/ and this report comes from one clean end-to-end `run.py all` of the final scripts. Its env phase dropped the t_drivers left by those iterations before anything else ran.
The LOCAL_URI password never appears in any script, output or this report; run.py scrubs the URI and password from every captured stdout and stderr.
